definition: John D. Lafferty is an American scientist, Professor at Yale University and leading researcher in machine learning.
details: He is best known for proposing the Conditional Random Fields with Andrew McCallum and Fernando C.N. Pereira.

explainer.lead: John D. Lafferty is an American artificial intelligence researcher. His work spans computer science.

contributions.name: He was elected Fellow of IEEE in 2007 "for contributions to statistical pattern recognition and statistical language processing".

timeline.what: Lafferty received a Ph.D. in mathematics from Princeton University, where he was a member of the Program in Applied and Computational Mathematics, under Edward Nelson in 1986.

He has also received numerous awards, including two Test-of-Time awards at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML) 2011 & 2012, classic paper prize of ICML 2013, and Test-of-Time awards at the Special Interest Group on Information Retrieval (SIGIR) 2014.
In 2017, Lafferty was appointed the John C. Malone Professor of Statistics and Data Science at Yale University.
